questions.q: A family that consists strictly of a father, a mother, and their children is referred to as a ____________.
questions.explain: A **nuclear family** is the basic family unit consisting only of parents (father and mother) and their direct offspring.

questions.q: Which of the following family members is part of the extended family rather than the nuclear family?
questions.explain: An **uncle** is outside the immediate parent-child unit, placing him in the extended family category, which also includes grandparents, aunts, and cousins.

questions.q: According to Ephesians 6:1-3, what is the primary duty of children towards their parents?
options: To provide financially for the parents
To obey and honor them in the Lord
To point out their parents' mistakes regularly
To dictate the rules of the house
questions.explain: **Ephesians 6:1-2** commands: 'Children, **obey your parents** in the Lord, for this is right. Honor your father and mother...'

questions.q: Apostle Paul instructs wives in Ephesians 5:22 to do which of the following regarding their husbands?
options: Compete with their husbands for leadership
Submit to their own husbands as to the Lord
questions.explain: In **Ephesians 5:22**, Paul writes, 'Wives, **submit to your own husbands**, as to the Lord.'

questions.q: In Colossians 3:21, fathers are instructed not to provoke their children. What is the biblical reason given for this?
options: Lest the children report them to the authorities
Because children will physically fight back
Because it will make the family poor
questions.explain: **Colossians 3:21** states, 'Fathers, do not provoke your children, **lest they become discouraged**.'

questions.q: According to 1 Peter 3:7, husbands are commanded to live with their wives in an understanding way and to show them ____________.
questions.explain: **1 Peter 3:7** commands husbands to live with their wives in an understanding way, showing **honor** to the woman as the weaker vessel, since they are heirs with them of the grace of life.

questions.q: Why is protecting and maintaining a good family name important for a Christian youth?
options: It gives them a license to break civil laws.
It fosters respect, trust in the community, and glorifies God.
It guarantees immediate wealth without working.
It automatically exempts them from school exams.
questions.explain: A good family name builds a positive reputation, which brings **respect and trust** from others and serves as a good testimony that glorifies God.

questions.q: In Ephesians 6:5-9, how are servants (or employees) commanded to perform their duties?
options: With a sincere heart, as doing it for Christ
By doing only the minimum amount required
questions.explain: Apostle Paul instructs servants to obey their masters with fear and trembling, in **sincerity of heart**, as they would obey Christ, not by the way of eye-service (**Ephesians 6:5-6**).

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT an expected Christian role of parents toward their children?
options: Providing basic necessities like food and shelter
Teaching them spiritual and moral values
Encouraging them to seek revenge against their enemies
questions.explain: Christian parents are expected to raise their children in the training and instruction of the Lord. **Seeking revenge** contradicts Christ's teaching on forgiveness and love.
